question: Does the deployed bounded semantic correction allow a fresh Ukrainian neutron-star request to pass fact review and produce a natural-speed 60-second video that passes final QA?
stop_conditions: Submit this ID once; never retry it.
Preserve ambiguous provider outcomes as terminal/unknown.
Stop at first factuality, source, relevance, quota, duration, alignment, render or machine-audit failure.
Keep natural-speed voice, relevant real photographs, exact duration and QA gates unchanged.
Stop media generation if /data free space falls below 100 MB.
This plan authorizes one request only.

actual.failure_boundary: duplicate-label repair after bounded availability-first photo searches
actual.failure: Initial photo plan repeated generic neutron-star labels. One repair selected two different Wikimedia files of the same Vela supernova remnant, so canonical subject uniqueness rejected them. No candidate was downloaded or visually inspected.

fix.description: Allow at most one additional duplicate-subject repair after the first completed structural repair still repeats canonical labels. Restrict each repair to new available anchor IDs; preserve strict failure when no distinct candidate or valid labels remain.
